etf.title: ETFs
etf.intro: Important for European investors: US-listed ETFs (SPY, QQQ) usually cannot be bought through an EU broker (PRIIPs rules — no KID document). Funds marked UCITS are the European equivalents, genuinely available in the EU — the rest serve as a market reference.

commodities.title: Commodities
commodities.intro: We track commodity prices through liquid commodity ETFs (e.g. GLD for gold) — a more stable data source than futures contracts. Commodities have no company fundamentals, so the score rests purely on technical analysis (trend, momentum, volatility).
commodities.empty: Could not load data. Try refreshing the page.

dividends.title: Warsaw Stock Exchange dividends
dividends.intro: Companies ranked by dividend score — calculated from payout history rather than a single snapshot. The score combines three areas: dividend safety (40%), payout continuity and growth (35%), and yield attractiveness (25%).
dividends.introTax: Yields are shown gross and net of Polish capital gains tax (19%) — what actually reaches a Polish investor's pocket.
dividends.notPayingNote: These companies do not pay dividends — they often reinvest profits into growth. That is not a flaw, just a different strategy.
dividends.noneMatch: No company meets the selected yield threshold.
dividends.disclaimer: The dividend score is an educational tool, not investment advice. A high dividend yield can signal risk rather than opportunity — which is why safety carries the most weight.

items.a: An app for analysing stocks, ETFs, commodities and crypto. It turns fundamental and technical indicators into a rating from 0 to 100 and shows what that rating is based on.
Yes. You can currently use it free of charge, with no card required. Some advanced tools may move to a paid plan in the future.

items.q: Does StockFlow tell me what to buy?
items.a: No. Scores, price ranges and rankings are educational analysis tools, not investment recommendations. You make your own decisions at your own risk.

items.q: Where does the data come from, and how current is it?
items.a: Crypto prices come live from Binance. Stocks, ETFs and commodities come mainly from Yahoo Finance, delayed by up to about 15 minutes. Exchange rates come from the European Central Bank.

Stocks from the US, the Warsaw Stock Exchange and major European exchanges, ETFs (including UCITS funds available to EU investors), commodities and crypto. Any other instrument listed on Yahoo Finance can be checked by entering its symbol.

We combine a dozen indicators: valuation relative to the sector, trend, momentum, volume and volatility. Each has its own weight. In the app you see which indicators raise or lower the result, and how much data was available.

A tool that shows the range the price could reach over 1 to 60 days and the chance of touching a level you choose. It does not predict a single price; it shows a distribution of possible scenarios. Every forecast is recorded and checked after the fact.

items.q: Can I import my portfolio from XTB?
items.a: Yes. In xStation, export the open positions report to a CSV file and upload it in the Portfolio tab. You will see a preview of the recognised positions before anything is saved.

For any instrument on your watchlist you set an upper or lower level. When the price crosses it, you get an email, at most one alert of each type per day. Alerts need an email address on your account.
Passwords are stored only in encrypted form, and your connection to the app is encrypted. We show no ads and use no tracking scripts.

items.q: Does it work on my phone?
items.a: Yes. StockFlow runs in the browser on phones and computers, with nothing to install.
Yes. The interface and descriptions are available in English and Polish. You can switch the language in settings.
